div.head: ECf 12.10 A 1
div.ab: Et qui modo dicuntur comites, qui tercium denarium super forisfacturam habent, tunc temporis consules uocabantur.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 639 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 12, 10, and numbers 12, 10 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 12, 10 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
div.ab: And those who are now called earls (comites), who have the third penny of the forfeiture, were at that time called consuls.
